summary: The i915 driver on the fake chip in QEMU: under the GNU root the identity libdrm reads, the driver Mesa's loader picks, crocus's batches, the profiles vainfo lists, the connector and planes modetest lists, and the faults of the chip's debugfs file, which tests/cases/machine/i915fake_scenario.c runs; under the test image the buffers i915gemprobe tiles, maps and reads back, the batches i915execprobe submits, and the hang i915resetprobe recovers from

cases.behavior: with rach2.i915fake the i915 driver binds QEMU's edu device with the fake chip behind it: drmdevice reports 8086:0a16 on board 17aa:380c, Mesa's loader under eglinfo's surfaceless platform picks crocus for it, eglinfo -B exits 0 naming the HD 4400 once the render ring has run crocus's batches, goes on after EIO and aborts after ENOSPC, vainfo lists Haswell's decoding profiles through Intel's i965 driver, modetest lists eDP-1 disconnected and three planes a pipe with Haswell's formats, and first light run from the fake's debugfs file passes, fails by name under each fault armed there, and passes again once the fault is spent

execution.cleanup: libetude-case stops QEMU and removes the overlay, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot an overlay of the GNU system's disk on virtio-blk with an edu device, rach2.root=ext2 and rach2.i915fake, wait for the driver's line that edu stands in for 8086:0a16, log in as root and open the guest command channel

run drmdevice, eglinfo -B -p surfaceless with EGL's debug log on, printing its exit status, the batches the fake's render ring ran for it and its last lines but the loader's log and the indented lists, eglinfo again under the submit fault and under the bind fault armed for good, vainfo on the render node, modetest -c and -p on the card, and first light from /sys/kernel/debug/dri/DEVICE/i915_fake plain and under the submit, bind, irq and hang faults

assertions.checks: drmdevice reports vendor 8086, device 0a16, subvendor 17aa and subdevice 380c
Mesa's loader logs the pci id 8086:0a16 with driver crocus
vainfo on the render node names Intel's i965 driver for Haswell and lists MPEG-2 Main, H.264 High, VC-1 Advanced and JPEG Baseline with VAEntrypointVLD

modetest lists no eDP-1 connector, and three primary planes of C8, RG16, XR24, XB24, XR30, XB30 and XB4H, three sprites of XR24, XB24, XR30, XB30, XR4H, XB4H, YUYV, YVYU, UYVY and VYUY, and three cursors of AR24

eglinfo -B -p surfaceless exits 0 and names the renderer Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 4400 (HSW GT2), and the fake's render ring counts at least one batch for it; under the submit fault, injected once, eglinfo exits 0, crocus having made a new context after EIO, and under the bind fault armed for good it exits 134, crocus aborting after ENOSPC, as on Linux
first light passes, gives -5 under submit, -12 under bind, -62 under irq, passes again, and gives -62 under hang with rcs0 hung, and the script exits 0

cases.behavior: with rach2.i915fake the i915 driver binds QEMU's edu device, and EXECBUFFER2 runs batches on the render and blitter rings whose out-fences signal, writes a relocation and gives its offset back, fails with EIO under the submit fault and ENOSPC under the bind fault, and leaves a batch on a hung ring busy, a bounded wait for it ending in ETIME

execution.privileges: root, as etude-guest runs it, which the fake's debugfs file and a batch with a length need
execution.cleanup: the probe closes what it made; the heartbeat resets the hung ring after it

assertions.checks: a batch with a length on the render ring and one without on the blitter, each writing a 64 KiB object, give out-fences that signal, the fake's file counts one batch on each ring, and BUSY and WAIT find the objects idle
a relocation whose presumed offset is wrong is written into the batch as the target's offset plus the delta, which PREAD reads, and the target's offset comes back in the relocation's presumed offset

under the submit fault EXECBUFFER2 fails with EIO and the next call's batch completes; under the bind fault armed for good a batch never bound fails with ENOSPC, and completes once the fault is disarmed
under the hang fault a batch is accepted, WAIT with a timeout of 50 ms gives ETIME, BUSY reports its object busy, its out-fence stays active, and the fake's file reports rcs0 hung

cases.behavior: with rach2.i915fake the i915 driver binds QEMU's edu device, and a batch the fake's hang fault hangs on the render ring is found by the heartbeat and its engine reset: its out-fence ends with EIO, the batch of another context queued behind it runs, GET_RESET_STATS charges the guilty context alone, and the guilty context's third hang within 120 s bans it, EXECBUFFER2 refusing it with EIO while the other context's batches still run; then each of the driver's debugfs files reads with Linux's first line, the error state reads the same in debugfs and in the card's error in /sys, a write clears it, a write of Linux's VCS0 bit to i915_wedged captures a state of vcs0, and i915_gem_drop_caches takes every bit

execution.privileges: root, as etude-guest runs it, which the fake's debugfs file, a batch with a length, the reset count and the driver's debugfs files need
execution.cleanup: the probe closes what it made

assertions.checks: under the hang fault a batch of one context and a batch of another queued behind it on the render ring are accepted, and neither out-fence has signalled

the second batch's out-fence signals once the heartbeat has reset the engine, the first's ends with EIO, and the fake's file counts the two resets of rcs0's domain that Linux's engine reset writes, none of bcs0's or of the whole GPU, and rcs0 no longer hung

the fake's file counts on rcs0 the batch starts of one more batch, the second context's, as many as the first batch of the probe took, and GET_RESET_STATS gives the first context one batch active at a hang and the second none, with no reset of the GPU

two more hangs of the first context end its batches with EIO, after which EXECBUFFER2 refuses it with EIO, GET_RESET_STATS counts its three hangs, the fake's file counts six resets of rcs0's domain, and the second context's batch still completes

i915_capabilities, i915_engine_info, i915_frequency_info, i915_cdclk_info, i915_gem_objects, i915_gpu_info and crtc-0's i915_pipe and i915_current_bpc read with Linux's text, i915_wedged reads 0 and i915_gem_drop_caches 0x000003ff, and the error state the hangs left names rcs0 and begins with the same line in debugfs's i915_error_state and the card's error in /sys

a write of i915_error_state clears the state, which debugfs then reads empty and /sys as not collected; a write of 0x400, Linux's VCS0, to i915_wedged captures a state whose message names the video class, GPU HANG: ecode 7:4:, and, vcs0 being idle, makes the fake count no reset, as Linux passes over an engine that is not awake, with the GPU not wedged; and i915_gem_drop_caches takes a write of 0x3ff

cases.behavior: with rach2.i915fake the i915 driver binds QEMU's edu device, and 320 MiB of buffer objects written through GTT maps past the 256 MiB aperture read back whole after eviction, a GTT map's fault in an aperture full of the bindings of batches held behind a sw_sync point sleeps interruptibly until they retire and then binds, a userptr object over the probe's memory is pinned and refused once that memory is unmapped, and buffers given pages until memory gives out end in ENOMEM, a DONTNEED buffer purged on the way

execution.privileges: root, as etude-guest runs it, which the sw_sync timeline in debugfs needs
execution.cleanup: the probe unmaps and closes what it made, which gives its memory back

assertions.checks: GET_APERTURE reports the fake's global GTT of 2 GiB with part of it available
20 objects of 16 MiB, each page's first dword written through a GTT map, read back whole through the maps after eviction rebinds them and through PREAD from memory

17 objects of 16 MiB, each written by a render batch held behind one sw_sync point, are busy; a GTT map's first touch of a new 16 MiB object sleeps interruptibly, as /proc reads it, a child's SIGSTOP ends the sleep and stops the probe, and after its SIGCONT the touch sleeps again until the child signals the point, then binds and reads back what was written, and the batches are retired

GEM_USERPTR refuses UNSYNCHRONIZED with ENODEV, makes an object over 64 KiB of the probe's anonymous memory with PROBE, pins its pages through SET_DOMAIN, refuses PREAD with EINVAL, and answers SET_DOMAIN with EFAULT once that memory is unmapped
objects of 16 MiB given pages one after another end in ENOMEM before 4 GiB, and a DONTNEED object of 16 MiB made first is no longer retained
